referenceFunction.generalComment: Inventory refers to the production of 1 kg hydrated ethanol 95% (dry basis, i.e. 1.05 kg hydrated ethanol 95% wet basis), respectively 1 kWh of electricity from wood (u=80%, i.e. 55% dry matter). The multioutput-process 'wood, in distillery' delivers the co-products 'ethanol, 95% in H2O, from wood, at distillery' and 'electricity, from wood, at distillery'. Economic allocation with allocation factor for common stages of 99.7% to ethanol. Allocation is done according to carbon balance for CO2 emissions.; UUID: 431a1a2d-aa33-305b-841a-06c8a6719eed
referenceFunction.includedProcesses: This dataset includes the transport of wood from the forest to the distillery, and the processing of wood (u=80%) to hydrated ethanol (95%) and electricity. System boundary is at the distillery. Dehydration to anhydrous ethanol is not included. Process heat and power supply is ensured by the combustion of unconverted solids.
referenceFunction.localName: xx Ethanol, 95% in H2O, from wood, at distillery
referenceFunction.name: xx Ethanol, 95% in H2O, from wood, at distillery

geography.text: Data is adapted to Swiss conditions from NREL ethanol process design from yellow poplar (1999)

technology.text: Ethanol is produced by dilute acid pre-hydrolysis and simultaneous saccharification and co-fermentation (SSCF) of lignocellulosic biomass. Process heat and power supply is ensured by the combustion of unconverted solids. Excess electricity is exported to the power grid.

timePeriod.text: Data from 1999 to 2006, pilot scale, near-future technology

representativeness.extrapolations: Direct emissions (resulting from the combustion of unconverted solids, incl. lignin) are based on the the combustion of wood chips (with emission control), according to the corresponding dry matter content, carbon content and energy content.
representativeness.productionVolume: Production volume of ethanol for use as a fuel was 1-1.5 Ml in 2005 in CH
representativeness.samplingProcedure: Data is adapted to Swiss conditions from NREL ethanol process design from yellow poplar, modelling by ENERS (CH)
